speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. To better understand the nature of your bleeding, have you noticed any bruising that appears easily without injury, or any bleeding from your gums? Also, does anyone in your family have a history of bleeding problems?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). Given the child's age and presentation of isolated thrombocytopenia symptoms (mucosal bleeding, petechiae, easy bruising) without history of family bleeding disorders, this is the most likely diagnosis. I will not ask further questions but recommend immediate platelet count and peripheral smear.
